issues.failure_explanation: With the test function $w(t) = e^{-t/T}\partial_t\psi(t)$, the quantity $(\partial_t\psi, w)_{J_T} = \int_0^T |\partial_s\psi|^2 e^{-s/T} ds$ is real and nonnegative (Eq. (3.14)), so $\mi(\partial_t\psi, w)_{J_T}$ is purely imaginary and $\mathrm{Re}(\mi(\partial_t\psi, w)_{J_T}) = 0$. The concluding display nevertheless counts this term as real, equating $\mathrm{Re}(\mi(\partial_t\psi,w) + \mu(\psi,w))$ with $\int|\partial_s\psi|^2 e^{-s/T} + \frac{\mu}{2T}\int|\psi|^2 e^{-s/T} + \frac{\mu}{2e}|\psi(T)|^2$; that identity is false, and even taken at face value it would force $\psi \equiv 0$ only for $\mu \ge 0$ (mixed signs for $\mu < 0$). The correct consequences of the test are: the real part gives $\mu\big(\frac{1}{2T}\int|\psi|^2 e^{-s/T} + \frac{1}{2e}|\psi(T)|^2\big) = 0$, whose bracket is nonnegative and vanishes only at $\psi \equiv 0$ (covering $\mu \neq 0$), while for $\mu = 0$ the imaginary part gives $\int|\partial_s\psi|^2 e^{-s/T} = 0$, hence $\psi \equiv 0$ via $\psi(0) = 0$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the final display by the separate conclusions of the real and imaginary parts (real part for $\mu \neq 0$, imaginary part for $\mu = 0$), using only Eqs. (3.14)-(3.15), which are correct.
issues.overall_effect: Only Proposition 3.2 is affected: its proof contains an invalid step, although its statement (continuous-level uniqueness for all $\mu \in \R$) is true. No later result cites Proposition 3.2.
issues.title: Invalid real-part evaluation in the uniqueness proof of Proposition 3.2
issues.why_classification: The statement survives in full; the repair is a short, local rearrangement of estimates already present in the proof, and there are no dependent results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: meaning that if $\xi \in \mathbb{C}$ is a root of $q^{\K^p(\rho)}$, then $\xi^{-1}$ is also a root

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed reciprocity ($\xi$ a root $\Rightarrow$ $\xi^{-1}$ a root) is false already for $p = 1$: there the interior bands give $q^{\B^1}(z) = -(z-1)^2$ and $q^{\bC^1}(z) = (z^2-1)/2$, so by definition (3.21) $q^{\K^1(\rho)}(z) = \mi q^{\B^1}(z) - \rho q^{\bC^1}(z) = -\mi(z-1)^2 - \frac{\rho}{2}(z^2-1)$, whose roots for $\rho = 2$ are $1$ and $\mi$, while $1/\mi = -\mi$ is not a root. The inference in the proof is invalid: $q^{\B^p}$ is palindromic and $q^{\bC^p}$ is anti-palindromic (both with real coefficients), so a nontrivial combination is neither palindromic nor anti-palindromic, and reciprocity does not follow. (Related misprints in the same argument: (3.25) drops the factor $\mi$ and the minus sign from (3.21), and the factored displays write $z^{-(p+j)} + z^{p+j}$ where $z^{-(p-j)} + z^{p-j}$ is required, producing spurious negative powers of $z$.) The consequence actually used downstream — that $q^{\K^p(\rho)}$ is of type $(\ell, 2p-2\ell, \ell)$ — is nevertheless true: the real palindromic/anti-palindromic structure yields $z^{2p}\overline{q^{\K^p(\rho)}(1/\bar z)} = -q^{\K^p(\rho)}(z)$ (self-inversive), so zeros are symmetric under $\xi \mapsto 1/\bar\xi$.

failure_location.quote: The symbol polynomial $q^{\mathbf{K}^p(\rho)}$ of the family $\{ \K_n^p(\rho) \}_n$ defined in \eqref{eq:21} is a reciprocal polynomial.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the symmetry as self-inversivity: from the real palindromic $q^{\B^p}$ and real anti-palindromic $q^{\bC^p}$, verify $z^{2p}\overline{q^{\K}(1/\bar z)} = -q^{\K}(z)$, conclude zeros are symmetric about the unit circle, hence type $(\ell, 2p-2\ell, \ell)$, and keep the rest of the argument unchanged; also correct (3.25) to $q^{\K} = \mi q^{\B} - \rho q^{\bC}$ and fix the exponents in the coefficient displays.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition 3.9 is false as stated and its proof does not justify the type count it is used for. Theorem 3.13, whose proof combines Propositions 3.9 and 3.12, and Theorem 4.2, which rests on Theorem 3.13, are unproven as written, though their conclusions are recovered once the symmetry argument is corrected.
issues.title: False reciprocity claim for the symbol polynomial (Proposition 3.9)
issues.why_classification: A labelled result's statement is false and its key inference must be replaced by a different (contained) symmetry argument; the repair preserves the proposition's used conclusion and the main theorem with no loss of scope or rates, so it is more than a routine fix but requires no new global architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For~$\rho>0$ and~$p \in \mathbb{N}$, the function $K_p(\theta,\rho)$ has exactly 2 simple zeros
Combining Propositions \ref{prop:39} and \ref{prop:312}, we obtain the main result of the paper.

issues.failure_explanation: Step 4 announces the goal of exactly two simple unit-modulus zeros for all $\rho \in \R$, but Proposition 3.12 — the only ingredient counting the zeros — is stated and proved solely for $\rho > 0$, and Theorem 3.13's proof is just 'Combining Propositions 3.9 and 3.12'. The gap is genuine: simplicity of the zero $\theta = 0$ uses $\lim_{\theta\to0}\partial_\theta K_p(\theta,\rho) = -\rho$, which vanishes at $\rho = 0$; indeed $K_p(\theta,0) = -B_p(\theta)$ has a double zero at $\theta = 0$ (since $B_p(\theta) \sim -c\theta^2$), so the 'two simple zeros' property and the bijection of Lemma 3.10 fail at $\rho = 0$, and no argument at all is given for $\rho < 0$.

failure_location.quote: Then, for all~$p \in \N$ and~$\rho \in \R$, the family of matrices~$\{\K_n^p(\rho)\}_n$ defined in~\eqref{eq:21} is weakly well-conditioned.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add two short supplements: for $\rho < 0$, the symmetry $K_p(-\theta,-\rho) = K_p(\theta,\rho)$ ($B_p$ even, $C_p$ odd) reduces to Proposition 3.12; for $\rho = 0$, $\K_n^p(0) = \mi\B_n^p$, whose weak well-conditioning is already cited in the paper (Prop. 3.10 of the companion paper, invoked in Theorem 4.2's proof), consistently with Theorem 3.8(b) applied with a double unit zero.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 3.13 is unproven for $\rho \le 0$. Negative eigenvalues of $\frac12\Delta + V$ do occur (in fact $\mu_j \to -\infty$), so the case $\rho = \mu h < 0$ is needed for the Schrödinger application; Theorem 4.2 only invokes $\mu_s = \sqrt{\mu_w} > 0$ and is not affected by this particular gap.
issues.title: Theorem 3.13 claims all $\rho \in \R$ but the zero-counting argument covers only $\rho > 0$
issues.why_classification: Both missing cases follow in one line each from facts already in the paper, and the full statement of Theorem 3.13 is preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we show that, for all $p \in \N$ and $\mu \in \R$, the condition number of~$\K_h^p(\mu)$, as a function of~$h$, does not grow exponentially but rather as an algebraic power of~$1/h$.
It is said to be~\textit{weakly well-conditioned} if~$ \kappa(\A_n) $ grows as a power of~$ n $.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper defines its stability goal as: for all $\mu \in \R$, $\kappa(\K_h^p(\mu))$ grows at most algebraically in $1/h$, with no relation between $h$, $p$, $\mu$. Since $\K_h^p(\mu) = h^{-1}\K_n^p(\mu h)$ with $n = T/h + p - 1$, fixing $\mu$ and letting $h \to 0$ corresponds to $\rho = \mu h \to 0$ along the family. What is actually proved (via Theorems 3.8-3.9 and the zero analysis) is weak well-conditioning of each family $\{\K_n^p(\rho)\}_n$ with $\rho$ fixed, i.e., along $\mu = \rho n/T \to \infty$. The two statements differ, and the cited Toeplitz bounds have symbol-dependent (hence $\rho$-dependent) constants: uniformity as $\rho \to 0$ cannot be taken for granted because the two simple unit zeros of the symbol coalesce into a double zero at $\rho = 0$. No uniformity or varying-symbol argument is given or cited, so the concluding sentence 'In other words, (3.10) is unconditionally stable' is unsupported; the analogous transfer to the fully discrete method (2.7) (Remark 3.2, abstract, conclusions) would in addition require simultaneous control over all modal parameters $\rho_j = \mu_{j,h_{\bx}} h$.

failure_location.quote:
In other words, the variational formulation in \eqref{eq:10} is
unconditionally stable.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a uniformity-in-$\rho$ conditioning analysis near $\rho = 0$ (and over the unbounded modal range for the full method), e.g., by quantifying the Amodio-Brugnano-type bounds in terms of the separation of the symbol's unit zeros; alternatively, restate the result as weak well-conditioning of the fixed-$\rho$ families and weaken the 'unconditional stability' claims accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The central advertised guarantee — unconditional stability of (3.10) and of the space-time method (2.7) in the sense the paper defines — is not established by the fixed-$\rho$ analysis; Theorem 4.2's stability conclusion for the wave-equation method inherits the same gap through its citation of Theorem 3.13.
issues.title: Per-fixed-$\rho$ conditioning does not deliver the advertised unconditional stability for fixed $\mu$
issues.why_classification: The gap can be closed by a contained new lemma built on the explicit symbol analysis already developed, without changing the guarantee type (any algebraic power suffices) or abandoning results; alternatively a limited restatement leaves a recognizably comparable result. It exceeds minor because a nontrivial missing argument must be supplied.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Moreover, Lemma \ref{lem:a1} implies that the corresponding family of Schur complements is weakly well-conditioned for all $\mu_s \in \R$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes polynomial conditioning of the Schur complements $\bS = \B_h^p + \mu_w \bC_h^p (\B_h^p)^{-1} \bC_h^p$ (via Lemma A.1, which bounds $\kappa(\bS)$ in terms of $\kappa(\bM)$ — the opposite direction of what is needed next) and then asserts that this 'implies the stability of formulation (4.2)', i.e., polynomial growth of the condition number of the full block matrix $\begin{pmatrix} \B & \bC \\ -\mu_w \bC & \B \end{pmatrix}$. That implication is not justified anywhere and is false for general block matrices. It holds here only through the block factorization $\bM = \begin{pmatrix} I & 0 \\ -\mu_w\bC\B^{-1} & I \end{pmatrix} \mathrm{diag}(\B, \bS) \begin{pmatrix} I & \B^{-1}\bC \\ 0 & I \end{pmatrix}$ together with $\|\bC_h^p\| = O(1)$ (Prop. 3.7(1)) and polynomial bounds for $\|(\B_h^p)^{-1}\|$ (weak well-conditioning of $\B$), none of which is written down.

failure_location.quote: By choosing~$\mu_s = \sqrt{\mu_w}$, the Schur complements for both matrices in~\eqref{eq:33} coincide. Hence, the weakly well-conditioning of these Schur complements implies the stability of formulation~\eqref{eq:30} for all $p \in \mathbb{N}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the block-factorization estimate $\kappa(\bM_w) \le \kappa(L)\kappa(U)\max(\kappa(\B), \kappa(\bS))$ with the triangular factors and their inverses bounded by $1 + \mu_w\|\bC\|\|\B^{-1}\| = O(\mathrm{poly}(n))$; all required bounds are already available in the text.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 4.2 — the paper's advertised verification-free stability proof for the first-order-in-time wave method of the companion paper — has an unjustified key step; the corresponding claims in the abstract and Section 4 preamble are unsupported as written.
issues.title: Weak well-conditioning of the Schur complement does not by itself imply stability of the wave formulation (Theorem 4.2)
issues.why_classification: The conclusion is correct and the missing estimate is a short, routine assembly of bounds already established in the paper; no claim needs weakening and there are no further dependents.

issues.failure_explanation: From the stated Schur decomposition $Q^H(\mi\B)^{-1}\bC Q = R$ one obtains the exact factorization $\mi\B\otimes\M + \bC\otimes\A = \mi\,(\B Q\otimes I)(I\otimes\M + R\otimes\A)(Q^H\otimes I)$, so the solution of (5.1) is $\Psi = -\mi\,(Q\otimes I)(R\otimes\A + I\otimes\M)^{-1}(Q^H\otimes I)(\B^{-1}\otimes I)F$. Algorithm 1 instead solves $(R\otimes\A + R^{-1}\otimes\M)Z = Y$ in step 4 (the mass block is coupled to $R^{-1}$ rather than to $I$, and the factor $-\mi$ is missing) and returns $\Psi = -(Q\otimes I)Z$ in step 5, which does not satisfy (5.1) — already in the scalar $1\times1$ case the two expressions differ. Hence the algorithm as written does not compute the solution of the system it is meant to solve.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change step 4 to solving $(\mathbf{R}^p_{h_t}\otimes\A_{h_{\bx}} + \mathbf{I}\otimes\M_{h_{\bx}})\boldsymbol{Z} = -\mi\,\boldsymbol{Y}$ (no need to form $R^{-1}$; still block upper triangular with spatial blocks $r_{ii}\A + \M$) and step 5 to $\boldsymbol{\Psi} = (Q\otimes I)\boldsymbol{Z}$.
issues.overall_effect: The stated solver fails its input-output contract; the surrounding efficiency claims (steps 2, 3, 5 are cheap; step 4 has block upper triangular structure) and the numerical experiments are not formally affected, since the corrected system has the same block-triangular structure.
issues.title: Algorithm 1 does not solve system (5.1) as written
issues.why_classification: The correction is forced by the stated Schur decomposition and preserves the algorithm's structure and every claimed guarantee; no formal result depends on the algorithm.
